newsitem.title: INDIA: Two Kashmir militants die in gunbattle with troops.
newsitem.headline: Two Kashmir militants die in gunbattle with troops.

text.p: Two separatist guerrillas died on Monday in a gunbattle with Indian paramilitary troops in the troubled region of Kashmir, a spokesman for the Border Security Force (BSF) said.
He said three militants were arrested, one of whom was seriously wounded in the attack in Srinagar, the summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir.
Separatist guerrillas lobbed a grenade at a police patrol near the Firdous Chowk area in the city. It exploded but caused no damage.
The blast came after a gunbattle erupted between separatist guerrillas and paramilitary forces conducting a cordon-and-search operation in the area, the spokesman said.
The BSF spokesman said the search operation was continuing.

The latest attack comes two days before Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan and his Indian counterpart Inder Kumar Gujral are scheduled to meet to try to resolve outstanding bilateral issues, including the hotly disputed issue of Kashmir.
The two countries have fought two of their three wars over the territory since both became independent from Britain 50 years ago.
The foreign secretaries ended four days of talks on March 31 and agreed to hold a subsequent round in Islamabad.
India, which controls two-thirds of Kashmir, accuses Pakistan of arming and training separatist guerrillas fighting New Delhi's rule in Jammu and Kashmir.
Pakistan, which rules the remaining one-third, says it only provides the separatists with political and diplomatic support.
More than a dozen militant groups are fighting New Delhi's rule for Kashmir's independence or merger with neighbouring Pakistan.
Police and hospitals say over 20,000 people have been killed in a seven-year-old rebellion in the Himalayan region.
